title: Display & monitors
blurb: Second monitor, docks, blurry or tiny text, flicker, projectors.

remedies.title: Second monitor not detected or shows "No signal"
remedies.why: A loose or wrong cable, the monitor set to another input, the adapter or dock not passing video, or the computer not looking for it.

steps.text: Check the monitor is on and set to the right input (HDMI 1, DisplayPort…) with its own buttons.
Reseat both cable ends, try another cable or port. USB-C ports only carry video if they have a display or Thunderbolt symbol.
Press Windows+P and pick Extend; then Settings › Display › Multiple displays › Detect.
Open Displays settings; hold Option and a Detect Displays button appears.
Base M1/M2 MacBooks drive only one external monitor (without special software).
Update the graphics driver.

remedies.title: Dock or USB-C hub not working (screens, network, USB)
remedies.why: The dock lost power, needs a firmware/driver update, or the laptop's port doesn't support everything the dock needs.

steps.text: Unplug the dock's power for 30 seconds, plug it back, then reconnect the laptop.
Use the laptop's Thunderbolt/USB-C port marked for display or the one the dock maker recommends.
Install the dock's driver or firmware update from its maker (DisplayLink docks need the DisplayLink app).
DisplayLink docks on a Mac need Screen Recording permission for the DisplayLink app.
Restart the laptop with the dock connected.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT the dock model and laptop model; some combinations need specific firmware.

remedies.title: Screen looks blurry, stretched or the wrong size
remedies.why: The resolution isn't the monitor's native one, or the cable/adapter limits it.

steps.text: Settings › Display › choose the monitor › Display resolution: pick the one marked (Recommended).
Displays › choose the monitor › pick "Default for display" or the sharpest option.
Old HDMI cables and cheap adapters cap the resolution or refresh rate; try a better cable.
Run ClearType text tuning for sharper text.

remedies.title: Text and icons are too small or too big
remedies.why: High-resolution screens need scaling to keep text readable.

steps.text: Settings › Display › Scale: try 125% or 150%. For text only: Accessibility › Text size.
Displays › choose a "Larger Text" size, or Accessibility › Display › Text size.
In browsers, Ctrl/⌘ and + makes one site bigger.

remedies.title: Screen flickers or goes black for a moment
remedies.why: A loose cable, refresh-rate mismatch, an app that clashes with the graphics driver, or failing hardware.

steps.text: Reseat or swap the cable.
Open Task Manager; if it flickers too, it's the display/driver, if not, an app causes it.
Set the refresh rate to the monitor's standard (often 60 Hz): Settings › Display › Advanced display.
Set the refresh rate in Displays to the monitor's standard.
Update the graphics driver.

remedies.escalate: If the laptop's own screen flickers with nothing connected, it may be a hardware fault: tell IT.

remedies.title: Screen looks yellow, too dim or changes brightness
remedies.why: Night Light/Night Shift warms the colours, and automatic brightness or battery saver dims the screen.

steps.text: Turn off Night light or set its schedule.
Turn off "Change brightness automatically" and content-adaptive brightness in Display settings.
Displays › Night Shift, and turn off "Automatically adjust brightness" and True Tone if colours shift.
Battery saver / Low Power Mode dims the screen; plug in or turn it off.

remedies.title: Show my screen on a projector or TV
remedies.why: The computer can mirror (same picture) or extend (extra desktop), by cable or wirelessly.

steps.text: Cable: connect HDMI, then press Windows+P and choose Duplicate (same picture) or Extend.
Wireless: Windows+K connects to Miracast TVs and adapters on the same network.
Cable: connect HDMI/USB-C; in Displays pick Mirror or Extended.
Wireless: Control Center › Screen Mirroring for AirPlay TVs and Apple TV.
In PowerPoint, Slide Show › Monitor chooses which screen shows the slides.

remedies.title: A window opened off the screen
remedies.why: The app remembers a monitor that's no longer connected.

steps.text: Click the app in the taskbar, then press Windows+Shift+Left or Right to move it to another screen.
Or press Alt+Space › Move, then any arrow key, and move the mouse to bring it back.
Choose Window › Move to … in the app's menu, or Window › Zoom; or hold Option while clicking the green button.
Changing the display arrangement briefly (Mirror, then back) also pulls windows home.
